chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said:

I asked him about a man who incurred janabah (major ritual impurity) during the night in Ramadan, then slept having known about it, and did not wake up until Fajr reached him. He said: 'He must complete his fast and make up one other day.' I said: 'If that is the case for the man while he is making up Ramadan?' He said: 'Let him eat on that day and make it up, for it is not like Ramadan in any of the months.'

key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: Major ritual impurity requiring full body wash (ghusl)
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The month of fasting in the Islamic calendar
key_terms.يَقْضِ: To make up for a missed obligatory act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one sleeps through Fajr in Ramadan while in a state of janabah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Samaanah ibn Mihran reports that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the validity of the fast and the obligation of compensation for those who sleep through Fajr in a state of janabah. The Imam clarifies that while the fast remains valid, the day must be made up (qada) as an ordinary day rather than a duplicate of Ramadan, implying that the specific spiritual merit of Ramadan is not replicated in the makeup fast. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that intentional delay of ghusl does not invalidate the fast itself, provided one intends to fast.
